newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh town under water as floods kill sixty.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh town under water as floods kill sixty.

text.p: As a giant Russian-made MI-8 army helicopter hovered over the Chittagong Hill Tracts on Sunday, the picturesque town of Bandarban hundreds of feet below looked like a vast pool of water.
A few buildings jutting out of the water and hundreds of people crowding their roofs were the only visible signs of life in the town of 50,000 people, surrounded by green hills on all sides.
Bandarban, a major town in the Hill Tracts in southeastern Bangladesh, was among areas devastated by current floods that have killed at least 60 people and made a quarter of a million homeless.
The helicopter carried senior army officers, including regional commander Major-General Abdul Matin, and a group of journalists, on a mission to survey the havoc.

Floodwater on Saturday filled the entire town of Bandarban, forcing thousands of residents to flee into the surrounding hills. Offices, business centres, police stations and army garrisons were evacuated.

"Two-thirds of the town's population are still stranded in their submerged homes while others have fled to nearby hills," Atiqul Islam Chowdhury, deputy commissioner of Bandarban district, told reporters after the helicopter landed in a small dry patch of land.
However, the situation was likely to improve soon as rain stopped and the floodwater started to recede slowly, he said.
Fatema Begum, among some 500 people gathered at a relief distribution centre in the town, said acute shortage of drinking water posed a serious health problem.
"Some people are already ill after they drank polluted water as all ponds and most tube-wells have submerged," the 50-year-old woman said.
Soldiers have joined relief and rescue operations after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Saturday asked them to reinforce efforts by the civil administration.
Helicopters were ferrying food and other supplies to areas where they can find a dry ground to land, one disaster management official said on Sunday.
"So far we have 60 confirmed deaths since the deluge began on Tuesday," one official in Chittagong said on Sunday.
"We are almost certain that 19 passengers missing in the Sangu river after their boat capsized on Saturday are also dead," he said.
The new deaths included six in Chakoria in Cox's Bazar district and seven in the Satkania and Rauzan areas in Chittagong, officials and police said.
Officials said the victims died in landslides, house cave-ins and by drowning.
Unofficial sources on Sunday put the death toll at nearly 75.

The floods, caused by heavy monsoon rain, left a quarter of a million people homeless, officials said. At least half a million people were reported marooned in their half-submerged homes as the floods afflicted 19 out of the country's 64 administrative districts.
Nearly 100,000 people have been shifted to flood shelters, and many more moved to higher ground on their own.
Road links between Chittagong and neighbouring districts, including Cox's Bazar and Bandarban, remained impassable as floodwater washed away several small bridges and partly inundated highways.
Train communications were disrupted because tracks were flooded or under threat. Handling of cargo at the Chittagong port also was hampered, port officials said.
The flooding has also disrupted communications with northeastern districts of Sylhet, Sunamganj and Habiganj.
At least 300,000 acres (120,000 hectares) of cropland, including tea districts, have been inundated, agriculture officials said, but they were unable to provide loss estimates immediately.
